ui_bugs.issue: GET /account (as a signed-in staff user via hard reload / SPA reload) served meta robots='index, follow' instead of the intended 'noindex, nofollow'. Root cause is that RequireAuth returns a <div data-testid='auth-loading'> during the async token re-hydration on a fresh page load — Account.jsx (which owns the noindex useSeo call) never mounts during that window, so the static index.html meta tags stay in place. Since /account is auth-gated, no external crawler will actually reach it (they'd get redirected to /signin, which correctly emits noindex), so the practical SEO risk is low, but it does violate the spec. Fix suggestion: also add useSeo({noindex:true}) inside RequireAuth's loading branch, or hoist the /account noindex to a route-level meta manager, or put a default 'noindex' robots tag directly in index.html and let public pages override it.

rca_of_the_issue: For /account noindex regression: On a hard-load of /account, AuthProvider needs a tick to hydrate the JWT from localStorage. During that tick RequireAuth returns a small <div data-testid='auth-loading'> placeholder — Account.jsx (which is where the useSeo({noindex:true}) lives) has not mounted yet, so the static <meta name='robots'> that ships in public/index.html (index,follow) is what's on the page. If Playwright/crawler snapshots that moment, it sees index,follow. Fix: put a global default noindex in index.html and let public pages set index via useSeo, OR add useSeo inside RequireAuth's loading branch.
